newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hovers at $20, US expiry, stocks in focus.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hovers at $20, US expiry, stocks in focus.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures danced around $20 a barrel on Tuesday, recovering some poise after sliding early amid talk of poor refining margins and a heavy delivery into the expiring NYMEX June contract, brokers said.
July Brent futures shed 17 cents to $19.99 a barrel by 1424 GMT, 15 cents above the session low.
But the expiry and thin volumes were making trading conditions choppy. Mixed views about U.S. inventory data due later on Tuesday were adding to the jumpy market, dealers said.
"People are looking at the expiry but the APIs are also making some people nervous," said one.
Last week's American Petroleum Institute (API) report showed crude stocks rose by a massive seven million barrels to stand nearly 23 million barrels above year-ago levels.

Some traders were expecting crude stocks to show a modest fall in the latest figures due after the market closes on Tuesday but gasoline stocks -- of particular importance as the driving season gathers pace -- may show little change.
Dealers were also nervous that the expiry of the June NYMEX crude contract could produce a repeat of last month, when a hefty two million barrels of crude were delivered against the May contract.
Technically, Brent looked fragile after breaching support at $19.93 although some brokers expected $19.85 to provide a prop.

While Brent futures have started to retrace some of last week's $1.40 gains, steady to firmer physical differentials for benchmark Dated Brent and other North Sea crudes have maintained the pressure on refining margins which has forced at least one refiner to cut crude throughput.
Meanehile, June IPE gas oil shed $1.50 to $176.25 a tonne, $1.25 above the session low. June/July slipped 25 cents deeper into contango.
